The Lord said to Aaron, “Look, I have given you charge of the offerings set apart for me. I have given you all the holy gifts of the Israelites as your anointed share, to you and your sons with you, as a lasting statute.”

This shall be the most holy portion from the fire: all their offerings, all their fine flour, all their sin offerings, and all their offerings that they present to me. They are most holy, for you and your sons.
You must eat it in a most holy place. Every male may eat it. It shall be holy to you.

This is the portion set apart from your gifts: I have given you all the offerings set apart by the Israelites, to you and your sons and daughters with you, as a lasting statute. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the oil, and all the best of the grain and wine—the firstfruits that they give to the Lord—I have given to you.
All the firstfruits of their land that they bring to the Lord shall be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
Everything devoted to God in Israel shall be yours.

Every firstborn that opens the womb, of all flesh that they offer to the Lord, whether human or animal, shall be yours. But you must redeem the human firstborn, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
From the age of one month onward, you must redeem them at a price of fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel. A shekel is twenty gerahs.

But you must not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats, because they are holy. Sprinkle their blood on the altar, and offer up their fat as an offering on the altar, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Their meat shall be yours. Like the breast set apart as an offering and like the right thigh, it shall be yours.

All the contributions of holy things that the Israelites set apart for the Lord I have given to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a permanent statute. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the Lord for you and your descendants with you.

The Lord said to Aaron, “You shall receive no inheritance in their land, and you shall have no share among them. Rather, your share and your inheritance among the Israelites shall be the Lord’s contributions and his holy things.”
“To the descendants of Levi I have given all the tithes of the Israelites as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform in the Tent of Meeting.
The Israelites must no longer approach the tent of meeting, lest they incur guilt and die.

The Levites shall perform the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they shall bear responsibility for their wrongdoing. This is a permanent statute throughout their generations. They shall receive no inheritance among the Israelites.
For I have given the Levites as an inheritance the tithes that the Israelites set apart for the Lord. That is why I have said to them that they shall receive no inheritance among the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:

Speak to the Levites and tell them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithes that I have given you from them as your inheritance, set apart from them a contribution to the Lord, a tenth of the tithes.
Your contribution will be credited to you like grain from the threshing floor and like a contribution from the winepress.
In this way you too shall set apart a contribution to the Lord from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. From them give the Lord’s contribution to Aaron the priest and his sons.
From all the gifts you receive, set apart the full contribution to the Lord, from all the best of them, the portion to be consecrated.
Tell them: When you set apart the best of it, it shall be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and the produce of the winepress.
You and the members of your households may eat it anywhere, because it is your wages in return for your service in the Tent of Meeting.
You will incur no sin on its account when you set apart the best of it. You must not defile the holy things of the Israelites, lest you die.”
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
This is the requirement of the law that the Lord commanded, saying: “Tell the Israelites to bring you a red cow, sound and without blemish, on which no yoke has been laid.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. It shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.
He shall burn the cow before him. He shall burn its hide, its blood, and its flesh, together with its dung.
The priest shall take cedarwood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and throw them into the fire in which the cow is burning.
The priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may enter the camp, but the priest shall remain unclean until evening.
The person who burns the cow shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he shall remain unclean until evening.

A man who is clean shall gather up the cow’s ashes and put them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept in reserve for the whole congregation of the Israelites, for the water of sprinkling, because it is a sin offering.
The person who gathers the cow’s ashes shall wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This shall be a permanent statute for the Israelites and for those who turn to me and live among you.
Anyone who touches the dead body of any human being will be unclean for seven days.
He must be sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day, and he will become clean. If he is not sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not become clean.

Anyone who touches the corpse of any human being who has died and is not sprinkled defiles the Lord’s tabernacle. That person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of sprinkling was not sprinkled on him, he will remain unclean; his uncleanness is still upon him.
This is the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent, and everyone who is in the tent, will be unclean for seven days.
Every open vessel that has not been sealed is unclean.
Anyone who touches someone killed by a sword in the open field, or a dead body, a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person, they must take some of the ashes from the burning of the sin offering and pour fresh water over them in a vessel.

A clean man must take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on the vessels, on all the people who were there, and on anyone who touched a bone, someone who was killed, a dead body, or a grave.

The clean person must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He must sprinkle him on the seventh day, and the unclean person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be clean in the evening.

But if a man is unclean and is not sprinkled, that person must perish from among his congregation, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. The water for sprinkling was not sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
This will be a law for you forever. Whoever sprinkles the water for sprinkling must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water for sprinkling will be unclean until evening.
Anything the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.
The Israelites, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Rekem. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the people to drink, and the people gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses and said to him, “If only we had died in the plague that killed our brothers before the Lord!
Why have you brought the Lord’s congregation into this wilderness, so that we and our livestock should die here?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt and bring us to this miserable place? It is no place for sowing seed, or for vines, fig trees, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.
Moses and Aaron went away from the congregation to the entrance of the tent of meeting. They fell on their faces, and the glory of the Lord appeared to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him,

Take the staff and gather the congregation, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. Bring water out of the rock for them, and give the congregation and their livestock water to drink.
Moses took the staff from before the Lord, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the whole congregation before the rock, and he said to them, “Listen now, you rebels! Shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. A great deal of water came out, and all the people and their livestock drank.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust me and show my holiness before the Israelites, you will not bring this congregation into the land I have given them.”
These are the waters of quarreling, where the Israelites quarreled before the Lord, and he showed himself holy among them.
Moses sent messengers from Rekem to the king of Edom: “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has overtaken us.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our ancestors.
We prayed to the Lord, and he heard our voice. He sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are at Rekem, a town at the edge of your territory.

Now let us pass through your land. We will not pass through fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from wells. Instead, we will travel along the king’s highway. We will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through my territory, or I will come out against you with the sword.”
The Israelites said to him, “We will go up along the road. If we or our livestock drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We will only pass through on foot.”
Edom said, “You shall not pass through.” Edom came out against them with a powerful army and a strong hand.
Edom refused to let the Israelites pass through its territory, so Israel turned away from it.
They set out from Rekem, and the Israelites, the whole community, came to Mount Hor.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom:

Aaron will be gathered to his people, for he will not enter the land I have given the Israelites, because you rebelled against the command of my mouth at the waters of strife and did not show my holiness at the waters before their eyes.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and die there.
Moses did as the Lord commanded him. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on Mount Hor, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
The whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, and the entire house of Israel mourned Aaron for thirty days.
When the Canaanite king of Geder, who lived in the south, heard that Israel was coming along the spies’ route, he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the Lord and said, “If you will indeed hand this people over to me, I will devote their towns to destruction.”
The Lord listened to Israel and handed the Canaanites over to them. They laid them waste and devoted them and their towns to destruction. They named that place Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. The people grew impatient on the journey.
The people grumbled against God and against Moses and said, “Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are sick of this meager bread.”
The Lord sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people. Many people of Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said to him, “We have sinned by grumbling against the Lord and against you. Pray before the Lord that he will remove the snakes from us.” So Moses prayed for the people.
The Lord said to Moses, “Make yourself a venomous snake of bronze and set it up as a sign. Everyone who is bitten by a snake shall look at it and live.”
Moses made a bronze snake and set it up as a sign. Whenever a snake bit someone, that person looked at the bronze snake and lived.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness facing Moab, to the east, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the valley of Zered.

From there they set out and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness extending from the territory of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the boundary of the Moabites, between the Moabites and the Amorites.
For this reason it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: “A flame in the whirlwind and in the valley of the Arnon.
He established the valleys that sloped toward the settlement of Ad and adjoined the border of the Moabites.”
There was the well, the well about which the Lord said to Moses, “Gather the people for me, and I will give them water.”
Then Israel sang this song: “Rise up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the leaders of the people hollowed out and opened with their staffs. From the wilderness it was given as a gift.
From Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth in the valley in the countryside of Moab, to the top of the height overlooking Jeshimon.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites and said to him,

“Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from the wells. Instead, we will travel along the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered his entire army and went out into the wilderness to meet Israel. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, because the border of the Ammonites was strongly defended.
Israel captured all these towns. Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land, from his border as far as the Arnon.
That is why those who speak in proverbs say: “Come into Heshbon! Let the city of Sihon be built and established.
For fire came out from Heshbon, and a flame from the stronghold of Sihon. It consumed Ar [?] of Moab and those who cultivated the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Arnon! Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh! He gave his sons as hostages and his daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites.
The fields of Heshbon perished as far as Ribon [?] and lay desolate as far as Nekah [?] in the wilderness.”
Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer. He captured its villages and destroyed the Amorites who were there.
They turned and went up to the land of Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet them, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

The Lord said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, because I am handing him over to you, together with all his people and all his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
They destroyed him, his sons, and all his people, leaving him no survivor, and they took possession of his land.
The Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
The Moabites were very afraid of the people because they were so numerous. The Moabites were distressed because of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this assembly will graze on everything around us, as an ox grazes on the green plants of the field.” Balak son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, who was by the River in the land of the Ammonites, to summon him and say to him, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land. They are now camped opposite me.

Now come and curse this people for me, because they are stronger than I am. Perhaps we will be able to destroy some of them and wipe them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with their divination fees in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s words.
He said to them, “Stay here tonight, and I will give you an answer according to what the Lord tells me.” So the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said to him, “Who are these men with you?”
Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent word to me, saying:
“Look, a people has come out of Egypt and covered the face of the land. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and destroy them.”
God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak’s leaders, “Go back to your own land, because the Lord is unwilling to let me go with you.”
The leaders of Moab got up, came to Balak, and said to him, “Balaam is unwilling to come with us.”
Balak again sent messengers, more important and distinguished than the earlier ones.
They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Do not hold back from coming to me.’”
“For I will honor you greatly and do whatever you tell me. Come and curse this people for me.”
Balaam answered Balak’s servants, “Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go against the word spoken by the Lord my God, whether in a small matter or a great one.”
Now you too stay here tonight, and I will find out what more the Lord will say to me.
God came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If these men have come to call you, get up and go with them. But do only what I tell you.”
Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
God’s anger burned against him because he went, and the angel of the Lord stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two young servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road, holding his drawn sword in his hand. The donkey turned off the road and went into the field, and Balaam beat the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
The angel of the Lord stood in a vineyard path, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
The donkey saw the angel of the Lord and pressed against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against the wall. So he beat her again.
The angel of the Lord went on farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn either to the right or to the left.
The donkey saw the angel of the Lord and lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he beat the donkey with a stick.
The Lord opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hands, I would kill you now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, whom you have ridden from your youth until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” He said to her, “No.”
The Lord opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road, holding his drawn sword in his hand. He bowed down and fell facedown in worship.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out to oppose you because you have directed your course against me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside before me, I would have killed you by now and kept her alive.”
Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned. I did not know that you were standing in the road to oppose me. Now, if this is wrong in your eyes, I will turn back.”
The angel of the Lord said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but do only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with Balak’s leaders.
Balak heard that Balaam was coming and went out to meet him at the city of Moab on the Arnon border, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Look, I sent for you to summon you. Why did you not come to me? Perhaps you thought that I did not have the power to honor you.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. But can I really say anything on my own now? I will speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”
Balaam went with Balak, who brought him to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak slaughtered cattle and sheep and sent some to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
When morning came, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he saw the outermost part of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him. Balaam and Balak offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offerings, and I will go. Perhaps the Lord will come to meet me. Whatever message he shows me, I will tell you.” And he went off quietly.
God appeared to Balaam, and he said to him, “I have prepared seven altars and offered bulls and rams on the altars.”
The Lord put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said to him, “Go to Balak and speak this way.”
He came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offerings, with all the officials of Moab.
He began his poem and said, “Balak, king of Moab, brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east. He said to me, ‘Come, curse Jacob for me; come, destroy Israel for me.’
How can I curse someone whom God has not cursed? How can I destroy someone whom the Lord has not destroyed?
For I see them from the mountaintops, and I look at them from the hills. Here is a people who live alone and are not counted among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a quarter of Israel? May I die the death of their upright people, and may my end be like theirs.
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I called you to curse my enemies, but here you are blessing them!”
Balaam answered, “Look, whatever the Lord puts in my mouth, that is what I am careful to speak.”
Balak said to him, “Come with me to another place, where you can see them from there. You will see only their outskirts, not all of them. Curse them for me from there.”
He took him to the lookout field, to the top of the hill. He built seven altars and offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offerings while I go over there.”
The Lord appeared to Balaam, put a message in his mouth, and said to him, “Go to Balak and say this to him.”
He came to him, and he was standing beside his burnt offerings, with the leaders of Moab beside him. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say?”
He took up his oracle and said, “Rise, Balak, and listen! Pay attention to my testimony, son of Zippor!
God is not a man who lies, nor a human being who changes his mind. He speaks and acts, and his word stands forever.
Look, I was brought here to bless, and I will not reverse the blessing.
I see no wrongdoing in Jacob, and I observe no trouble in Israel. The Lord their God is with them, and praise for their king is among them.
God, who brought them out of Egypt in his strength and majesty.
For there is no sorcery in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. At this time it will be said to Jacob and Israel, ‘What God has done!’
Look, a people rises like a lion and lifts itself up like a lion. It will not lie down until it eats its prey and drinks the blood of the slain.
Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all.”
Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you that whatever the Lord tells me, that is what I do?”
Balak said to Balaam, “Come, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God, and you can curse them for me from there.”
Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks Jeshimon.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him, and offered bulls and rams on the altars.
Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel. He did not go to seek omens as he had done each time before, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam lifted his eyes and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He took up his poetic declaration and said, “Balaam son of Beor declares; the man whose eye is open declares.”
The one who hears the word of God declares, the one who sees a vision of God, fallen down with his eyes open.
How beautiful is your tent, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel!
Like flowing streams, like a garden beside a river, like a tent the Lord has planted, and like cedars beside the water.
A man will come forth from his sons, and his offspring will be by abundant waters. He will be exalted above King Agag, and his kingdom will be raised high.
God brought them out of Egypt by his strength and his majesty. He will devour the nations that are his enemies, break their bones, and cut through their loins.
He crouched and lay down like a lion, like a lion cub. Who will rouse him? Those who bless you are blessed, and those who curse you are cursed.
Balak's anger flared against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, but here you are blessing them—three times now!”
“Now get out and go home! I said I would greatly honor you, but the LORD has kept you from receiving honor.”
Balaam answered Balak, “I also told the messengers you sent to me,
Even if Balak gives me his house full of silver or gold, I cannot go against the word from the Lord's mouth and do good or evil on my own initiative. Whatever the Lord tells me, that is what I say.
Now, look, I am going back to my own land. But come, let me advise you about what this people will do to your people in the days to come.
He took up his poetic declaration and said, “Balaam son of Beor declares; the man whose eye is open declares.”
The declaration of one who hears God's word, who knows the knowledge of the Most High and sees a vision of God, lying prostrate with his eyes open.

I have seen him, but not now; I have looked upon him, but he is not near. A star will rise from Jacob, and a leader will arise from Israel. He will destroy the warriors of Moab and subdue all the descendants of Seth.
Edom will become his possession, and Seir, the possession of his enemies, will become his. Israel will grow strong.
He will come down from Jacob and destroy anyone who escapes from the city.
He saw Amalek and took up his oracle, saying, “Amalek was the first of the nations, but in the end it will perish forever.”
He saw the Kenites and took up his oracle, saying, “Your dwelling is secure, and your nest is set in the cliff.
“If Kain is given over to burning, they will take you captive as far as Assyria.”
He took up his oracle and said, “Alas! Who will live when God brings these things about?”
Legions will come out from the land of the Kittim. They will subdue Assyria and will also subdue the Hebrews. They too will perish forever.
Balaam got up, turned back, and went to his own land. Balak also went on his way.
Israel stayed at Shittim, and the people began to engage in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
The women invited the people to the sacrifices offered to their gods. The people ate and bowed down to their gods.
Israel joined itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD’s anger burned against the Israelites.
The Lord said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and expose them before the Lord, facing the sun, so that my fierce anger may turn away from the Israelites.”
Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill those of his men who have joined themselves to Baal of Peor.”

Then an Israelite man came and approached in front of his fellow Israelites, and went in to a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and the whole assembly of the Israelites. They were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw him. He rose from among the assembly and took a spear in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman through her belly, in the chamber. Then the sudden plague was stopped among Israel.
Those who died in the sudden plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my anger away from the Israelites. He was zealous with my own zeal among them, so I did not destroy the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore I have said: Look, I am giving him a covenant of peace.
It will be for him and his descendants after him a covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.
The name of the slain Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the head of an ancestral household of the tribe of Simeon.
The name of the Midianite woman was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He was the leader of a clan of her ancestral family in Midian.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Harass the Midianites and destroy them,

For they harass you with the schemes they devised against you in the affair of Peor and in the affair of Cozbi, daughter of the rulers of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the sudden plague in the affair of Peor.
And it happened after the sudden plague.
The LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest:
Take a census of the whole assembly of the Israelites, from twenty years old and upward, according to their ancestral households, everyone in Israel who goes out to serve in the army.
Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan at Jericho.
Moses counted them from twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and the Israelites who had come out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben was Israel's firstborn. The descendants of Reuben: Hanoch, the clan of Hanoch; Pallu, the clan of Pallu.
Hezron, the clan of Hezron; Carmi, the clan of Carmi.
These were the clans of Reuben, and their number was forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.
The sons of Eliab were Nebuel, Dathan, and Abiram, prominent men of the assembly who rebelled against Moses and Aaron with Korah's assembly and rebelled against the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah when the assembly perished, when fire consumed two hundred and fifty men. They became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon according to their clans: Jemuel, the clan of Jemuel; Jamin, the clan of Jamin; Jachin, the clan of Jachin.
Zerah, the clan of Zerah; Shaul, the clan of Shaul.
These are the clans of Simeon: twenty-two thousand two hundred.
The descendants of Gad according to their clans: Ziphion, the clan of Ziphion; Haggi, the clan of Haggi; Shuni, the clan of Shuni.
Ozni, the clan of Ozni; Adi, the clan of Adi.
Arodi, the clan of Arodi; Adiel, the clan of Adiel.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad, according to their count: forty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah according to their clans were: Shelah, the clan of Shelah; Perez, the clan of Perez; Zerah, the clan of Zerah.
The sons of Perez were: Hezron, the clan of Hezron; Hamul, the clan of Hamul.
These are the clans of the sons of Judah, according to their count: seventy-six thousand five hundred.
The sons of Issachar according to their clans: Tola, the clan of Tola; Puah, the clan of Puah.
Jashub, the clan of Jashub; Shimron, the clan of Shimron.
These were the clans of Issachar according to their census: sixty-four thousand three hundred.
The descendants of Zebulun according to their clans: Sadar, the clan of Sadar; Elon, the clan of Elon; Nahaliel, the clan of Nahaliel.
These are the clans of Zebulun, according to their count: sixty thousand five hundred.
The sons of Joseph according to their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: Machir, the clan of Machir. Machir fathered Gilead. Gilead, the clan of Gilead.
These were the sons of Gilead: Iezer, the clan of Iezer; Helek, the clan of Helek.
Ashdiel, the clan of Ashdiel; Shechem, the clan of Shechem.
Shemida, the clan of Shemida; Hepher, the clan of Hepher.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad’s daughters were Mahlah, Noa [?], Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh and their count: fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
The sons of Ephraim, by their clans: Shuthelah, the clan of Shuthelah; Becher, the clan of Becher; Tahan, the clan of Tahan.
And these were the descendants of Shuthelah: Edan, the clan of Edan.
These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim, numbering 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The sons of Benjamin, by their clans: Bela, the clan of Bela; Ashbel, the clan of Ashbel; Ahiram, the clan of Ahiram.
Shupham, the clan of Shupham; Huppim, the clan of Huppim.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: Ard, the clan of Ard; Naaman, the clan of Naaman.
These were the descendants of Benjamin, numbering 45,600.
The descendants of Dan according to their clans: Shuham, the clan of Shuham. These were the clans of Dan according to their clans.
The entire clan of Shuham numbered 64,400.
The sons of Asher, by their clans: Imnah, the clan of Imnah; Ishvah, the clan of Ishvah; Ishvi, the clan of Ishvi; Beriah, the clan of Beriah.
The descendants of Beriah: Heber, the clan of Heber; Malchiel, the clan of Malchiel.
The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
These were the clans of the descendants of Asher, numbering 53,400.
The descendants of Naphtali according to their clans: Nahziel, the clan of Nahziel; Guni, the clan of Guni.
Jezer, the clan of Jezer; Shillem, the clan of Shillem.
These were the clans of the descendants of Naphtali, by their clans. Their number was 45,400.
The total number of Israelites counted was 601,730.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
The land shall be divided among these as an inheritance according to the number of names.
For the larger groups, increase their inheritance, and for the smaller groups, reduce their inheritance. Each is to receive his inheritance according to the number counted.
But the land must be divided by lot. They shall inherit it according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
The inheritance shall be divided by the decision of the lot between the larger and smaller groups.
These were the Levites counted by their clans: Gershon, the clan of Gershon; Kohath, the clan of Kohath; Merari, the clan of Merari.
These were the clans of the Levites: the clan of Libni, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of Mahli, the clan of Mushi, and the clan of Korah. Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam to Amram.
Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.
Their number was 23,000, counting every male a month old and older. They were not counted among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These were those counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Among these there was not a single man from those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said about them, “They will surely be killed in the wilderness, and not one man among them will remain, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.”

The daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clan of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noa [?], Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole assembly at the entrance to the tent of meeting and said,
“Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the assembly that rose up against the LORD in Korah’s assembly. Rather, he died for his own sins, and he had no sons.
Why should our father’s name be forgotten within his clan because he has no son? Give us an inheritance among our father’s brothers.”
Moses brought their case before the Lord.
The Lord said to Moses.
“The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. Give them a possession and an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and establish their father’s inheritance for them.
“And tell the Israelites: When a man dies and has no son, give his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his paternal uncles.
If he has no uncle, give his inheritance to his nearest relative within his clan, and he shall inherit it. This shall be a legal statute for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of Abarim and look at the land of Canaan, which I have given to the Israelites.
See it, and then you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered.

Because you rebelled against my command in the wilderness of Zin, when the assembly quarreled, and did not show me to be holy at the waters before their eyes.” These are the waters of quarreling at Rekem in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke before the Lord and said,
May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation.
“Who will go out before them and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the LORD’s assembly will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
The LORD said to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man who has the spirit in him, and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole assembly, and commission him before their eyes.
Give him some of your honor, so that the whole assembly of the Israelites will obey him.

He is to stand before Eleazar the priest and ask him for a decision through inquiry before the Lord. At his command they are to go out, and at his command they are to come in—he and all the Israelites with him, and the whole congregation.
Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole congregation.
He laid his hand on him and commissioned him, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him,
Command the Israelites and tell them: They must take care to present my offerings, the food of my offerings and the pleasing aroma, to me at their appointed times.
Tell them: This is the offering you are to present to the Lord: two year-old lambs without defect each day, as a regular whole burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning, and offer the other lamb at twilight.
And one-tenth of a seah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
This is the regular whole burnt offering established at Mount Sinai, an offering to the Lord with a pleasing aroma.
Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin of wine for each lamb. In the sanctuary, a drink offering of aged wine is to be poured out before the Lord.
Offer the other lamb at twilight. Offer it with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the Sabbath day, offer two year-old lambs without defect, and two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, together with its drink offering.
This is the whole burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular whole burnt offering and its drink offering.
At the beginning of your months, present whole burnt offerings to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without defect.
For each bull, offer three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and for each ram, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil.
For each lamb, offer one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering—a whole burnt offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

Their drink offerings are to be wine: half a hin for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. This is the whole burnt offering for the beginning of each month throughout the months of the year.
Also offer one young male goat as a sin offering to the Lord. It and its drink offering are to be offered in addition to the regular whole burnt offering.
On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Lord's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that month is a festival. Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
The first day is a sacred assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
Present an offering of whole burnt offerings to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs. They must be without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil. Prepare three-tenths of an ephah for a bull and two-tenths of an ephah for a ram.
Offer one-tenth of a seah for each lamb. Do this for all seven lambs.
Also offer one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
You shall offer these in addition to the morning whole burnt offering, the regular whole burnt offering.

You are to do this every day for seven days, presenting an offering of food with a pleasing aroma to the Lord. It and its drink offering are to be offered in addition to the regular whole burnt offering.
On the seventh day you shall have a sacred assembly. You shall do no ordinary work.
On the day of the firstfruits, when you present fine flour from the new harvest to the Lord at your Festival of Weeks, you are to hold a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
Present whole burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull and two-tenths of an ephah for each ram.
And one-tenth of a seah for each lamb; do the same for all seven lambs.
And one male goat to make atonement for you.
You are to offer these, without defect, together with their drink offerings, in addition to the regular whole burnt offering and its grain offering.
On the first day of the seventh month, you are to hold a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work. It is to be a day of trumpet blasts for you.
Offer whole burnt offerings with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of an ephah for the bull and two-tenths of an ephah for the ram.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

These are in addition to the whole burnt offering for the beginning of the month and its grain offering, and the regular whole burnt offering, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings as prescribed—an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the tenth day of this seventh month, you are to hold a holy assembly. You must not do any ordinary work.
Present whole burnt offerings to the Lord with a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without defect.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of a measure for a bull and two-tenths of a measure for a ram.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all seven lambs.
Also one male goat as a sin offering, besides the burnt offering of atonement, the regular whole burnt offering, and their grain offerings and drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, you shall have a holy assembly. You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days.
Present a whole burnt offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering is to be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths of a measure for each bull, for all thirteen bulls, and two-tenths of a measure for each ram, for both rams.
And one tenth of a measure for each lamb, for all fourteen lambs.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering, its fine-flour offering, and its drink offering.
On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And the grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to their number, as prescribed.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat for sin, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.
And on the eighth day you shall gather together, and you shall do no ordinary work.
Present whole burnt offerings, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one young bull, one ram, and four year-old lambs without blemish.
And their fine flour offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular whole burnt offering with its fine flour offering and its drink offering.

These you shall offer to the Lord at the times of your festivals, besides your vowed offerings and your voluntary offerings, your whole burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your sacrifices.
And Moses told the Israelites everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites and said to them, "This is what the Lord has commanded:
When a man makes a vow to the Lord or swears an oath and binds himself to an obligation, he shall not break his word. He shall do everything that has come from his mouth.
And when a woman makes a vow to the Lord and binds herself to an obligation while she is young and in her father's house,
If her father hears her vows and the obligations she has bound herself to, and her father says nothing to her, all her vows and all the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand.
But if her father cancels them on the day he hears of them, none of her vows or the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand. The Lord will forgive her, because her father canceled them.
And if she marries while under her vows or a pledge spoken by her lips by which she has bound herself,
If her husband hears and says nothing to her on the day he hears, all her vows shall stand, and the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand.
But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears, her vows and the pledges spoken by her lips, by which she bound herself, shall be canceled. The Lord will forgive her.
And as for the vow of a widow or a divorced woman, everything to which she binds herself shall remain binding on her.
If she made a vow in her husband's house, or bound herself by an obligation under oath,
If her husband hears and says nothing to her and does not cancel them, all her vows shall stand, and all the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand.

But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears, nothing spoken by her lips concerning her vows and the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand, because her husband canceled them. The Lord will forgive her.
Her husband may confirm or cancel all her vows and all her binding oaths to deny herself.

But if her husband continues to say nothing to her from day to day, all her vows and all the obligations she has bound herself to shall stand, because her husband said nothing to her on the day he heard.
But if he cancels them after he has heard them, he will bear her guilt.
These are the laws the Lord commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father's house.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites, and afterward you will be gathered to your people.”
Moses said to the people, "Arm some men from among you for battle, so that they may go against the Midianites and carry out the Lord's vengeance on the Midianites."
Send a thousand from each tribe, from all the tribes of the Israelites, into the army.”
From the thousands of the Israelites, a thousand from each tribe were chosen: twelve thousand men armed for battle.

Moses sent them out, a thousand from each tribe, twelve thousand armed men, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, in the army. He carried the sacred vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They fought against Midian as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian along with the others they killed: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five Midianite kings. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian and their dependents captive, and plundered all their animals, all their livestock, and all their possessions.
They burned all the towns where they lived and all their encampments.
They carried away all the captives and all the plunder, both people and livestock.

They brought the captives, the captured animals, and the plunder to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole assembly of the Israelites, to the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly went outside the camp to meet them.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had returned from the military campaign.
Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the females alive?”

For these women became a stumbling block to the Israelites through Balaam’s advice, so that they rebelled and acted unfaithfully against the LORD in the affair of Peor, and a sudden plague struck the LORD’s assembly.
Now kill all the boys, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep alive for yourselves all the young girls who have not slept with a man.

But you must camp outside the camp for seven days. Anyone who has killed a person or touched someone who was killed must be sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
Sprinkle all clothing, every leather article, everything made of hair, and every wooden article.
Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had returned from battle, “This is the requirement of the law that the LORD commanded Moses:
“However, gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—
Everything that can go into the furnace, pass through fire, and it will be clean. Sprinkle it also with the water for sprinkling. Everything that cannot pass through fire, immerse in water.”
Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. After that, you may enter the camp.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“You, Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the ancestral families of the assembly must count the captured animals and the captives, both people and animals.
Divide the plunder between the fighting men who went out with the army and the whole congregation.
Set aside a levy for the LORD from the fighting men who went out with the army and from the whole assembly: one in fifty of the people, cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the Lord’s contribution.
From the Israelites’ half, take one in fifty of the people, donkeys, cattle, sheep, and all the animals, and give them to the Levites who attend to the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The plunder and captives that the people and the army had taken amounted to 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
The people, consisting of women who had not had sexual relations with a male, numbered thirty-two thousand in all.
The half that was the share of those who went out with the army amounted to three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep.
The levy for the Lord from the sheep was 6,750.
There were 36,000 cattle, and their levy for the Lord was 720.
There were 30,500 donkeys, and their levy for the Lord was 610.
There were 16,000 people, and their levy for the Lord was 320 people.
Moses gave the silver of the Lord’s contribution to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
From the Israelites’ half, which Moses had allotted to them from the men who had gone out with the army.
The congregation's half of the flock amounted to three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred.
And 36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 people.
Moses took one in fifty of the people and animals from the Israelites’ half and gave them to the Levites who attended to the duties of the LORD’s tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The men appointed over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, approached Moses.
They said to Moses, “Your servants have counted the fighting men in the army under our command, and not one man is missing from among us.
We have brought an offering to the LORD, each man bringing the gold articles he found—anklets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces—to make atonement for our lives before the LORD.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it crafted objects.
All the gold of the contribution that they set aside for the LORD, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, amounted to sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
But the soldiers had taken plunder, each for himself.

Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
The Reubenites and the Gadites had a very great number of livestock. They saw that Jazer and the land of Gilead were suitable places for livestock.
The Reubenites and the Gadites came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the assembly.
“Ataroth, Ribon [?], Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sheba, Nebo, and Beon—
The land that the Lord laid waste before the Israelites is land suitable for livestock, and your servants have livestock.
They said, “If we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants as an inheritance. Do not make us cross the Jordan.”
Moses said to the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad, “Will your brothers go out to battle while you stay here?
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from crossing into the land that the Lord has given them?
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land.
They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they discouraged the Israelites from entering the land that the Lord had given them.
The Lord's anger burned against them that day, and he swore, saying:
‘The men who came up from Egypt, twenty years old and older, shall not see the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they have not followed me wholeheartedly.’
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, who followed the Lord wholeheartedly.’
The Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation of men who had done evil in the Lord’s sight had died out.
And look, today you too have risen up in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to increase the Lord’s anger against Israel again.
If you turn away from the Lord, he will again make you wander in the wilderness, and you will bring destruction on this whole people.”
They approached him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and towns for our families.
“We ourselves will arm ourselves and go ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them into their own land. Our families will stay in fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
We will not receive an inheritance with them on the other side of the Jordan or beyond, because we have received our inheritance on the eastern side of the Jordan.”
Moses said to them, “If you do this and arm yourselves for battle before the Lord,
and all of you cross the Jordan, armed for battle before the Lord, until he destroys his enemies before him,
and the land is subdued before the Lord, then you may return, free of obligation to the Lord and to Israel. This land will be yours as an inheritance before the Lord.
But if you do not do this, you will be sinning against the Lord. Know that your sins will catch up with you.”
Build towns for your families and pens for your flocks, and do what you have promised.
The descendants of Reuben and Gad said to Moses, “Your servants will do as our lord commands.
Our families, our wives, our possessions, and all our livestock will remain in the towns of Gilead.”
Your servants will cross over, armed for battle, before the Lord, as our lord has said.
Moses gave instructions concerning all of them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral tribes of the Israelites.

Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad cross the Jordan with you, armed for battle before the Lord, and the land is subdued before you, give them the land of Gilead as an inheritance.”
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they will receive their inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.”
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad answered Moses, “We will do just as the Lord has told your servants.
We will cross over into the land of Canaan, armed for battle before the Lord, but our inherited possession will be on this side of the Jordan.”

Moses gave the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: all the land and its towns within its borders, and the towns of the surrounding land.
The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, and Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran—fortified towns—and pens for the flocks.
The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
And Nebo and Baal-meon, whose names had been changed, and Sibmah. They gave names to the towns they had built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, conquered it, and destroyed the Amorites who were there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them the Villages of Jair, as they are called to this day.
Nobah went and captured Kenath [?] and its villages, and named it Nobah after himself.
These are the stages of the journeys of the Israelites, who came out of the land of Egypt in their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Moses recorded their departures and the stages of their journeys at the Lord’s command. These are the stages of their journeys and their departures.
They set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. After the Passover, the Israelites came out of Egypt boldly, in full view of all the Egyptians.
The Egyptians were burying the firstborn whom the Lord had killed among them. The Lord also carried out judgment against their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and camped at Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped in front of Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and went through the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days through the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there beside the water.
They set out from Elim and camped beside the Red Sea.
They set out from beside the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim. There was no water there for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Ekrona and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, which is Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the Lord’s command and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites left the land of Egypt, on the first day of the first month.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Geder, who lived in the south in the land of Canaan, heard when the Israelites came.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iye-abarim and camped at Ribon-gad.
They set out from Ribon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped at Mount Abarim, opposite Nebo.
They set out from Mount Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan at Jericho.
They camped beside the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimon as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho.
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
You must destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. You must destroy all their objects of worship and all their cast images, and tear down all their high places.
You will take possession of the land and settle in it, because I have given you the land to possess.

Take possession of the land by lot according to your clans. Give a larger inheritance to the larger groups and a smaller inheritance to the smaller groups. Each must receive the place where the lot falls for him. They must inherit according to their ancestral tribes.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land before you, those of them who remain will become spikes in your eyes and thorns in your temples, and they will trouble you in the land where you live.
And I will do to you what I intended to do to them.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites and tell them: You are entering the land of Canaan. This is the land that will be divided among you as an inheritance—the land of Canaan within its boundaries.
Your southern side will extend from the wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. Your southern boundary will begin at the eastern end of the Salt Sea.
Your boundary will turn south of the ascent of Sepharvaim and pass on to Zin. It will extend south of Rekem of Gaia, go out to Hazar-addar, and pass on to Azmon.
The boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt, and it shall end at the sea.
Your western boundary shall be the Great Sea and its coastline. This shall be your western boundary.
This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out a boundary to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor you shall mark out a boundary to the entrance of Hamath, and the boundary shall extend to Zedad.
The boundary will go out to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. These will be your northern boundaries.
You shall mark out your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The boundary will go down from Shepham to Diblah, east of Ain. The boundary will continue downward and reach the eastern shore of the Sea of Chinnereth.
The boundary will go down to the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, with its boundaries all around.
Moses commanded the Israelites and told them: This is the land you must divide by lot, which the Lord commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For the tribe of Reuben according to their ancestral families, the tribe of Gad according to their ancestral families, and half the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, there to the east, toward the sunrise.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
These are the names of the men who will assign the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Take one leader from each tribe to divide the land among you.
“These are the names of the leaders of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
From the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Ammihud.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon.
From the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli.
From the tribe of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Nahaliel son of Ephod.
From the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
From the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
From the tribe of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan.
From the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
From the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.”
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to assign the Israelites their inheritance in the land of Canaan.
The Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho and said to him:
Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from the inheritance they possess. They must also give the Levites the pasturelands surrounding those towns.
The towns will be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands will be for their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the towns you give the Levites must extend a thousand cubits outward from the town wall all around.

Measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand cubits on the south side, two thousand cubits on the west side, and two thousand cubits on the north side, with the town in the middle. This will be the open land belonging to your towns.
Among the towns you give the Levites, six must be cities of refuge for you, where someone who has killed his neighbor unintentionally may flee. In addition to these, give forty-two towns.
All the towns you give the Levites will total forty-eight towns, together with their open lands.

As for the towns you give from the Israelites’ inheritance, take more from those who have more and fewer from those who have less. Each must give towns to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance he receives.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
Prepare cities to serve as your cities of refuge, so that someone who kills a person accidentally may flee there.
These towns shall be places of refuge for you from the avenger of blood. The killer shall not be put to death until he stands before the assembly for judgment.
The towns you give shall be six cities of refuge for you.
Set aside three towns beyond the Jordan, and set aside three towns in the land of Canaan. They shall be towns of refuge.
For the Israelites, for anyone who turns to me, and for those who live among you, these six towns shall be places of refuge, so that anyone who kills a person accidentally may flee there.
If he strikes someone with an iron implement so as to cause death, and that person dies, he is a murderer. That murderer must be put to death.
If someone strikes another person with a stone held in his hand in a way that could kill him, and he dies, he is a murderer. He must be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a wooden implement in his hand so as to cause death, and that person dies, he is a murderer. He must be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
If he struck him out of hatred, or threw something at him deliberately, and he died, he is a murderer.

If, out of hostility, he strikes someone with his hand so as to cause death, and that person dies, he is a murderer. He must be put to death. The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer when he encounters him.
But if someone suddenly strikes another person without hostility, or throws any implement at him without malicious intent,
Or if, without seeing someone, he throws any stone capable of killing at him, and that person dies, though he was not his enemy and did not wish him harm.
the assembly shall judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to these rulings.

The assembly shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood, and the assembly shall send him back to the town of refuge to which he had fled. He shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city of refuge to which he fled,
If the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundaries of the town of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the killer, he incurs no bloodguilt.
For this reason, he shall live in the town of refuge until the high priest dies. When the high priest dies, the killer may return to the land of his inheritance.
These laws shall remain in force for you forever, throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Whenever anyone kills a person, the killer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses. A single witness shall not testify against a person to have that person put to death.
Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves death. He must be put to death.
You shall not accept a bribe allowing someone who flees to a town of refuge to go and live in the land before the high priest dies.

You shall not pollute the land in which you live, for blood pollutes the land. No atonement can be made for the land in which blood has been shed unless the blood of the one who shed it is shed there.
You shall not defile the land in which you live, where I dwell, for I am the LORD, who dwells among the Israelites.

The heads of the ancestral households of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clan of Manasseh son of Joseph, came forward. They spoke before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the assembly, the heads of the ancestral households of the Israelites.

They said, “The LORD commanded our lord to give the land to the Israelites as an inheritance by lot. Our lord was also commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

If they become wives of men from another of the tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken away from their fathers’ inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribes into which they marry. It will be taken away from our allotted inheritance.

If a jubilee takes place for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribes into which they marry, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of their fathers’ tribe.”
Moses gave the Israelites this command at the LORD’s word: “The tribe of the descendants of Joseph is right in what it says.
This is what the LORD has commanded concerning Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry whomever they please, but they must marry within the tribe of their father’s clan.
The inheritance of the Israelites shall not pass from one tribe to another. Rather, the Israelites shall each hold on to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.

Every daughter who inherits property from any of the tribes of the Israelites shall become the wife of someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, so that the Israelites may each possess their ancestral inheritance.
No inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another. Rather, the tribes of the Israelites shall each hold on to their own inheritance.”
Zelophehad’s daughters did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and [?], the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their paternal uncles.
They became wives of men from the clan of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the LORD commanded through Moses for the Israelites on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
